issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepts NumericLiteralSegment with zero test coverage exercising that branch.
issues.detail: The OneOf now permits NumericLiteralSegment as a DEFAULT_LANGUAGE value, but the added create_login.sql fixture only exercises the naked-identifier (us_english) case. Either add a fixture like DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033 to pin the numeric branch in the YAML hash, or drop the NumericLiteralSegment alternative. Untested parser surface rots.

issues.description: IDENTITY grammar now accepts a sign on both seed and increment without a test or comment recording the intent.
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar is added before both NumericLiteralSegments. The PR title mentions only negative seed, yet increment also accepts a sign. If both are intentional (which matches MS docs), add fixtures covering IDENTITY(-1,-1), IDENTITY(-1,1), IDENTITY(1,-1) and a one-line comment stating the invariant. Otherwise tighten the grammar.

issues.description: DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT delimited list permits mixing COLUMN and CONSTRAINT items, which T-SQL forbids.
issues.detail: The new Delimited shape under DROP does not enforce homogeneity, so 'DROP COLUMN a, CONSTRAINT b' parses despite being invalid T-SQL. Split into two top-level alternatives (one COLUMN-delimited, one CONSTRAINT-delimited) so the parser does not over-accept, and add a fixture pinning the correct shape.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor from Delimited(OneOf) to bare OneOf silently narrows accepted syntax to one action per statement.
issues.detail: Previously the top-level grammar allowed comma-delimited alter actions; the new grammar allows exactly one, with Delimited pushed inside DROP. This matches T-SQL but is a real behavior change. Add a one-line comment stating the invariant ('one action per ALTER TABLE; multi-drop handled inside') so future readers don't treat it as a typo.

issues.description: Deleting the multi-action alter_table.sql fixture loses coverage instead of converting it to a negative test.
issues.detail: The removed ADD+DROP statement was invalid T-SQL, so removal is correct, but it also erased the record of that fact. Replace it with an expect-parse-error fixture so future grammar churn cannot quietly re-admit the malformed shape. Removing a case loses the fact; an unparsable fixture records it.

issues.description: AlterTable grammar is one large anonymous OneOf where each action shape should be a named segment.
issues.detail: ~150 lines of nested Sequence/OneOf/Bracketed inline the shape of every alter action. Extracting AlterTableDropColumnsSegment, AlterTableDropConstraintsSegment, and AlterTableSetSegment would make the OneOf a short list of references, each independently testable and reusable. The current form will accrete further on the next tweak.

synthesis.summary: Four independent T-SQL grammar fixes are bundled together — table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, signed IDENTITY values, and ALTER TABLE DROP lists. The headline cases have fixtures, but the panel agrees several new grammar branches shipped untested or under-tightened: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric values have no fixture, IDENTITY now accepts a sign on the increment with no test or commit note, and the new DROP delimited shape lets COLUMN and CONSTRAINT items mix in violation of T-SQL. The ALTER TABLE refactor is a deliberate narrowing worth a comment, and the deleted multi-action fixture should be replaced with a negative test. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — tighten the grammar and add the missing fixtures before merge.
